digest.component_or_area: rebar bridge surface — library, MCP, and CLI integration
propositions: Noun-based bridge operations (bridge_preview, bridge_sync, bridge_status, bridge_pause, bridge_resume, bridge_check_access) must be exported through the public library and registered as MCP tools using the shared canonical run_pass / _Disposition core without duplication or subprocess invocation.

Legacy rebar.reconcile(mode=...) and bridge_fsck() must remain callable with unchanged signatures, defaults, return types, exceptions, and mutation boundaries while internally delegating to the new shared helper.

New bridge MCP tools must have explicit typed inputs without mode vocabulary and publish outputSchemas; existing reconcile(mode=...) and bridge_fsck tools must retain their published schemas so older clients do not fail negotiation.

Every new structured-result MCP tool and public library function must use the shared canonical policy from prerequisite tickets (9895 disposition mapping, 4a44 mode-to-cap selection, b69c status snapshot, 1104 pause CAS) rather than reimplementing mode/exit-code tables.
mcp.allow_jira_sync must gate every mutating route (bridge_sync, bridge_pause, bridge_resume, mutating legacy reconcile modes) while not gating preview, status, fsck, or access-check read operations.

Compatibility adapters must preserve legacy mutation boundaries and defaults such that preview never silently becomes sync, and all mode mappings (reconcile-check/dry-run to preview, bootstrap modes to capped sync, live to uncapped sync) remain sourced from the closed prerequisite policy.
